channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: The Florida Times-Union’s Ryan O’Halloran reports Chris Rodriguez “has been cleared and will do individual work” in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Rodriguez underwent foot surgery in the offseason and missed all of OTAs and minicamp. He is ready to go for training camp, but the team is taking things slowly and holding him out of team drills for now. The extra reps should give second-year back Bhayshul Tuten a small leg up in terms of Week 1 carries, but this ultimately projects as a two-man committee to start the year.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Browns are hosting Jadeveon Clowney for a visit.
item.description: Clowney inked a one-year deal with the Cowboys last offseason and totaled 8.5 sacks. He has become the league’s preeminent gun for hire on defense, posting at least eight sacks with four different teams. The last time Clowney spent more than one year on a roster was from 2021 to 2022 in Cleveland. After trading Myles Garrett this offseason, the Browns could certainly use some extra firepower at EDGE.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Tucker Kraft (knee)said he will probably come off the active/PUP list “very soon.”
item.description: Kraft said all the way back in June that he would likely begin training camp on the PUP list. He added that he may simply need some time to get his conditioning right before taking the field, and his comments from today seem to confirm that. He was on pace to finish as the TE4 before suffering a torn ACL last year. Even if he starts slow in 2026, Kraft appears to be a safe bet for high-end fantasy production this year.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Tank Dell (knee) will be limited in practice for a few weeks.
item.description: Dell is still working his way back from the catastrophic knee injury that cost him all of the 2025 season. All reports on his health heading into training camp have been positive, but a slow ramp-up period could mean he isn’t playing a full-time role in Week 1. Jayden Higgins appears to be locked in for No. 2 duties in Houston with Dell, Xavier Hutchinson, and an injured Jaylin Noel all vying for the third spot in 11-personnel. Dell is likely the best bet of the three, but it’s more likely than not that there is no clear winner ahead of Houston’s opener.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Jaylin Noel (finger) will be out “a couple of weeks.”
item.description: The Texans placed Noel on the NFI list at the start of camp. He is unable to practice until the team activates him. For a second-year player who struggled to earn playing time as a rookie, this is far from ideal. Tank Dell isn’t fully participating in practice yet, meaning Xavier Hutchinson and Jayden Higgins will see plenty of reps with the first-team offense to start camp.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Bucs signed Ifeatu Melifonwu, formerly of the Dolphins, to a one-year contract.
item.description: Melifonwu signed a one-year deal with Miami last offseason and went on to appear in 16 games for the Phins, eight of which were starts. He intercepted one pass and recorded one sack. Melifonwu is a depth option at this point in his career, but he should still see some snaps on defense plus work on special teams with the Bucs.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: The Athletic’s Joe Person reports Chris Brazzell suffered a “moderate LCL tear in his left knee and is expected to miss up to eight weeks.”
item.description: The Panthers’ season starts in less than seven weeks, so it’s safe to assume Brazzell won’t be on the field for their opener. As a rookie, the lack of training camp reps will also be more meaningful for him. Brazzell was supposed to contend with Xavier Legette for the final starting role in three-receiver sets, but that is now out of the question. He is no longer on the season-long radar for fantasy purposes, though dynasty managers can still leave a light on for some late-season production.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Browns signed Grant Delpit to a three-year, $48 million contract extension.
item.description: Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the deal includes $35 million guaranteed. Delpit was set to play out the final year of his current contract in 2026 before landing this new deal. He totaled four pass breakups, one intercpetion, and a career-high three sacks in 2025. Though the pass-rushing production is unlikely to hold up this year, Delpit is a versatile safety on a defense that traded Myles Garrett in the offseason. Keeping him around beyond 2026 made sense for both sides.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Bran Bresee is “feared to have suffered a torn ACL.”
item.description: Bresee will undergo testing to confirm the diagnosis, but it’s safe to assume he is done for the year. He broke out with 7.5 sacks in 2024, but that number fell to 2.5 last year. Bresee is also a liability against the run, so his value largely comes from his production as an interior pass-rusher. The Saints picked up his fifth-year option this offseason, meaning he will remain with the team for the 2027 season before hitting free agency.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Giants GM Joe Schoen said Malik Nabers has been “running, cutting, running routes, and taking part in individual drills” during practice.
item.description: Nabers avoided the PUP list to start training camp, which was a bit of a surprise given the generally negative reporting surrounding his knee injury during the offseason. He suffered a torn ACL and meniscus, both of which required surgery. Nabers also underwent a cleanup procedure during the summer. Though he is still a long way away from fully participating in practice, all signs point to him playing early in the season, if not Week 1 outright.-Kyle Dvorchak
